I can especially answer any questions you may have about how to get started in property development, setting up your own business, being a landlord, being a property developer, how to find out property values, how to do your own surveying, conveyancing pitfalls, hiring contractors, how to fit out houses for lets... I will answer as best as I can!

If you haven't seen Homes Under The Hammer, it is a daytime TV show in the UK which follows people who buy properties at auction and renovating them for rental or to sell for a profit. This is essentially what we do.
My husband and I quit our jobs and are now making money from Homes Under The Hammer- style property development in the UK (mostly in the North of England) - AMA
How would a nOOb (such as I) get into such things, someone who had ZERO experience of property?

When you say zero experience, what do you mean? Have you ever bought a house? Have you never lived on your own? What is your level of competency with DIY? Can you only change a lightbulb or have you got any confidence in that. If you literally have no experience at all, you will need a very competent builder to be your project manager on the ground and you need to add about 10% to your budget, but the best things you can do to start is familiarise yourself with property prices in the areas you want to operate in. Register with a few auction houses and use websites such as zoopla, rightmove and mouseprice to compare property values/yields and how much auction properties sell for. Check the costs of jobs on something like The Building Sheriff. Ask people who have done large projects for recommendations for a builder. Buy yourself some good basic power tools so that you can at least start practicing and watching the professionals. Start watching youtube videos on how to fix common problems a) so you can identify them and b) so that you will be able to fix them in the future. Work out where the cash is going to come from and how much you will need- I suggest that for a small house in the North for a complete refurb with nothing structural you need approx £60k.

What has been the hardest challenge you two have faced?

Also how did it feel when you quit both your jobs & risked going into this business not knowing if it would pay off?

The hardest challenge has been having to neglect our own house to make money on these properties. As a back story- we were able to go into this business due to an inheritance of about £100,000 which came from my grandparents. Shortly after my grandmother died we were both working fairly good jobs and we had bought a house to renovate for us to live in about a year previously. Knowing we would have the cash due to this inheritance, we completely gutted our own house, chipped all the plaster off the walls, had it rewired and replumbed with bare plaster walls and bare floorboards. Not long after I found out I was pregnant. At the time my OH was in the army, and was actually in afghanistan for pretty much the duration of my pregnancy (yes, he is the dad!) and wanted to come out of the army when he got home. We looked at our finances and realised that if I returned to work I would barely make minimum wage after childcare costs, and my husband would end up working very long hours on probably less money than the army. He has been very good at DIY and construction jobs for a while now and wanted to make a go of this. We decided to use my inheritance money to start this business so that we could have the life we wanted rather than having to beg our employers for time off for school plays and dental appointments like I've seen my friends do. This has meant living in what is virtually a building site ourselves (with a baby!) in order to spend the cash and time on properties which have made money. It's been hard and upsetting, especially when I was full of hormones and we had no heating in winter time. I have to keep reminding myself though that we just have to suffer a small amount of discomfort for a lifestyle that most people with a 9-5 job would envy. I don't know if it is arrogance or just good preparation but we were always fairly confident in making money, and my OH has always said if necessary he will go back to the army. The properties we have bought have been chosen really carefully, and as we own them outright it's unlikely, barring a complete property crash, that we will lose money on them. I still get nervous about the money, as it's the most money I've ever had and it's for our son's future, but I'm pretty confident that it won't be a bad investment.

With regards to property development, if you could tell your previous selves (before you got involved in property development) anything to better prepare your future/present selves, what would it be? (Apologies if wording is awkward - felt like I was quoting Bill & Ted)

You won't stay motivated on your own. Our first property was a real slow start until my husband hired someone to do all the crappy jobs he didn't want to do, like filling the skip or sweeping up. Before that he was on his own trying to do everything and not getting very far with it. We've said over and over again we wish we'd hired her earlier.
